summary: Edge refill-offset causing scheduled webhook callbacks to receive 429s during SSL termination migration
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Streamlyr reports intermittent 429 throttles affecting scheduled webhook callbacks for their ingestion workers after we migrated SSL termination for the us-east edge pool. The pattern looks like short, repeatable 429 bursts at the top of scheduled windows (cron-aligned webhooks).

Impact:
- ~20% of webhook callbacks from Streamlyr in prod-us-east receive 429s for 2-10s bursts during scheduled job start windows.
- Jobs retry but the customer reported duplicate processing and longer completion times for nightly pipelines.

Environment:
- Redwood: hosted dedicated pool (Streamlyr dedicated tenant), prod-us-east edge pool, rate-limiter v3.2.1
- Customer: Streamlyr ingestion workers, scheduled cron at :00 and :15, long-lived webhook connections with short parallel fanout (10-40 concurrent connections).

Steps to reproduce (provided by customer):
1) Configure scheduled worker to issue 40 parallel callbacks to Redwood webhook route at exact minute boundary (:00)
2) Observe short 429 spikes lasting ~5s at start of window (seen in customer telemetry and our ingress logs)
3) Repeat after toggling SSL termination to origin (customer observed fewer 429s)

Observed behavior:
- Edge proxy shows refill-window offset for a subset of persistent connections after SSL termination migration (timestamps misaligned by 1s-3s across edge/ingress accounting).
- Rate-limiter token accounting appears to double-debit for around 2-3s for some connections (edge counted request, origin also counted during NAT/conn handover), causing tenant token bucket exhaustion and 429s.

Expected behavior:
- A single request should be accounted once per logical API call. Scheduled simultaneous starts should be smoothed by burst credit and not produce short tenant-wide 429s for customers within their burst allowances.

Relevant logs/metrics excerpts (redacted):
- ingress-edge-us-east-01 | 2026-03-10T00:00:00.001Z | INFO | conn_id=xyz req_id=abc accounting=INCR tenant=streamlyr tokens=40
- ingress-origin-us-east-02 | 2026-03-10T00:00:00.002Z | INFO | conn_id=xyz req_id=abc accounting=INCR tenant=streamlyr tokens=40
- rate-limiter | 2026-03-10T00:00:00.004Z | WARN | tenant=streamlyr token_bucket_exhausted 429_count=38

Temporary workaround recommended to customer:
- Stagger scheduled worker startups by 3-5 seconds
- Use per-route burst pool (we can enable a separate low-latency burst pool for webhook routes) until we fix cross-edge counting

Customer requests:
- Explanation of why migration increased 429 incidence and definitive remediation plan.
- Guidance on configuration to avoid short windows of throttling without sacrificing throughput.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Support (Asha): Opened with logs and customer reproduction steps. Customer says failures started after our SSL termination migration on 2026-03-09.

2026-03-10 11:03 - SRE (Diego): Initial hypothesis: accounting duplication during connection handover between edge TLS terminator and origin (NAT/conn reuse) — scheduling peaks amplify effect. Added rate-limiter and proxy traces for next 24h.

2026-03-10 14:22 - Customer (Streamlyr - Emily Zhao): We applied a temporary 3s stagger and saw successful reduction in 429s. Would like a configuration approach (console or API) to prevent this without changing cron timings.
2026-03-11 08:45 - Support (Asha): Requested SRE to confirm whether token increments are idempotent and whether duplicative accounting is possible across edge/origin boundary.

2026-03-11 12:30 - SRE (Diego): Found edge proxy behavior where connection reuse delayed origin-side accounting; introduced unique request-id header now being honored by both layers. Hypothesis: missing dedupe on accounting events during the migration path. Created PR to add accounting dedupe by request-id and a short debounce window (PR linked).
2026-03-12 10:00 - ENG (Lina Chen): Rolling out hotfix to rate-limiter to ignore duplicate increment events within 500ms if they share request-id and tenant. Will monitor for impact.
investigation_notes: Collected pcap-level timings for edge <-> origin handoffs for 10 reproductions; observed ~1.2-2.8ms variance leading to double-accounting race during token refill epoch boundary.

Reviewed rate-limiter refill epoch code: refill window aligns to epoch start of host handling the request. When SSL termination is moved to edge, the origin was still registering accounting events during a migration replay path.
Hypothesis: migration introduced an extra accounting path via legacy health-probe or connection-proxy resends that are counted separately when many parallel conns start simultaneously.
Simulated load with staging edge config: enabling per-route burst pool eliminated burst 429s for same workload; indicates isolation is effective as a mitigation.
Telemetry: token_bucket_refill_delay metric spiking around migration windows; alerts tuned to detect refill_offset > 8ms for prod us-east.
Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/1123 (dedupe accounting), ticket INT-330 to add telemetry for duplicate-accounting counts.
Customer-reported side-effect: duplicate webhook retries when their worker does naive retries; recommended idempotency key usage and exponential backoff.
Next step: coordinate with infra to push hotfix to us-east edge pool and verify with Streamlyr on a controlled 40-concurrency test at :00 UTC on 2026-03-13.
resolution: (pending) Hotfix rolled to staging and scheduled for canary in prod us-east on 2026-03-13. Temporary customer mitigation accepted (staggering or per-route burst). After canary, will validate with Streamlyr on controlled schedule. Follow-up: create console option to enable per-route burst pools and document guidance for cron-aligned workloads.
resolution_notes: Hotfix will ignore duplicate accounting events within 500ms for same request-id and tenant.
Ops to monitor rate-limiter duplicate-accounting metric and 429 rate for Streamlyr tenant for 48h after rollout.
Postmortem doc created and linked to Confluence page (see related_confluence_pages).
